papers.title: Sketch2TikZ: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning for Converting Hand-Drawn Sketches to Executable TikZ
papers.abstract_en: Automatic digitization of hand-drawn sketches into editable formats is crucial for modern document workflows and LaTeX integration. Converting sketches into executable TikZ code provides a structured representation of diagrams, but remains challenging due to noisy and ambiguous inputs, which hinder reliable interpretation and limit the effectiveness of token-level supervision for ensuring global diagram validity. To address these challenges, we propose Sketch2TikZ, a reinforcement learning framework that optimizes sketch-to-code generation via a sequential multi-reward strategy, combining Code-Structure ($\mathcal{R}_{cs}$), OCR ($\mathcal{R}_{ocr}$), CleanDIFT ($\mathcal{R}_{cd}$), and Self-Similarity ($\mathcal{R}_{ss}$) rewards to enforce textual, visual and structural correctness. We evaluate Sketch2TikZ on the SkeTikZ and FlowChart-3B benchmarks using metrics including compilation success rate (CSR), image similarity, code similarity, and character similarity. Our method achieves near-perfect compilation success and improves visual and textual alignment over strong open-source baselines, while remaining competitive with proprietary GPT-based vision-language models. Extensive ablations demonstrate that curriculum-based reward scheduling is critical for reducing reward interference, stabilizing training and mitigating proxy over-optimization. Overall, our results highlight the effectiveness of reference-aware, multi-objective reinforcement learning for structured diagram generation from noisy sketches.
papers.abstract_zh: 将手绘草图自动数字化为可编辑格式对现代文档工作流和 LaTeX 集成至关重要。将草图转换为可执行的 TikZ 代码可提供图表的结构化表示，但由于输入存在噪声和歧义，这一任务仍具挑战性，这些因素阻碍了可靠解释，并限制了 token 级监督在确保整体图表有效性方面的作用。为应对这些挑战，我们提出 Sketch2TikZ，一个强化学习框架，通过顺序多奖励策略优化草图到代码的生成，结合 Code-Structure（$\mathcal{R}_{cs}$）、OCR（$\mathcal{R}_{ocr}$）、CleanDIFT（$\mathcal{R}_{cd}$）和 Self-Similarity（$\mathcal{R}_{ss}$）奖励，以强制实现文本、视觉和结构正确性。我们在 SkeTikZ 和 FlowChart-3B 基准上使用编译成功率（CSR）、图像相似度、代码相似度和字符相似度等指标评估 Sketch2TikZ。我们的方法实现了接近完美的编译成功率，并在视觉和文本对齐上优于强开源基线，同时与专有 GPT 基视觉语言模型保持竞争力。大量消融实验表明，基于课程的奖励调度对于减少奖励干扰、稳定训练和缓解代理过度优化至关重要。总体而言，我们的结果凸显了参考感知的多目标强化学习在从噪声草图生成结构化图表方面的有效性。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 Sketch2TikZ 强化学习框架，用 Code-Structure、OCR、CleanDIFT 和 Self-Similarity 四种奖励的顺序多奖励策略将手绘草图转为可执行 TikZ 代码，在 SkeTikZ 和 FlowChart-3B 上实现接近完美的编译成功率。
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, posing challenges for existing architectures. Standard Transformers accumulate layer-wise, token-level KV caches, incurring linear GPU memory growth and quadratic computational complexity as the context expands. In contrast, linear-time architectures compress history into fixed-size states, but struggle to retain fine-grained details. We introduce MemOnce, a foundation architecture that learns scalable memory states for language models. MemOnce is based on two core designs: (a) Memory encoder-decoder: it caches only a small subset of final-layer hidden states as compact memory representations and dynamically decodes them back into KV caches for attention layers; (b) Memory sparse attention: for each continual input, MemOnce adaptively retrieves relevant memory representations, with the sparse indices computed only once across layers. Coupling these two designs enables efficient on-the-fly memory loading and KV cache decoding, drastically reducing the GPU memory footprint and achieving linear-time complexity. We conduct extensive experiments to show that MemOnce outperforms Transformers and other architectures across varying model sizes, context lengths, and training paradigms (pretraining and post-training adaptation). In particular, adapting Qwen3.5-4B with MemOnce reduces memory state cache by 1313$\times$ and prefill latency by 6.9$\times$ at 1M context, and improves throughput by 3.5$\times$ and overall memory performance by +5.77%. Finally, MemOnce generalizes zero-shot to downstream representation tasks, achieving competitive results against specialized models.
papers.abstract_zh: 在长时程和持续交互中部署大语言模型（LLM）需要为未来推理维护可复用的记忆状态，这对现有架构构成挑战。标准 Transformer 累积逐层、token 级的 KV 缓存，随着上下文扩展导致 GPU 内存线性增长和二次计算复杂度。相比之下，线性时间架构将历史压缩为固定大小状态，但难以保留细粒度细节。我们提出 MemOnce，一种为语言模型学习可扩展记忆状态的基础架构。MemOnce 基于两个核心设计：（a）记忆编码器-解码器：仅缓存最后一层隐藏状态的一小部分作为紧凑记忆表示，并将其动态解码回注意力层的 KV 缓存；（b）记忆稀疏注意力：对于每个持续输入，MemOnce 自适应检索相关记忆表示，稀疏索引仅跨层计算一次。结合这两种设计可实现高效的即时记忆加载和 KV 缓存解码，大幅降低 GPU 内存占用并实现线性时间复杂度。我们进行大量实验表明，MemOnce 在不同模型规模、上下文长度和训练范式（预训练与后训练适配）下优于 Transformer 和其他架构。特别是，用 MemOnce 适配 Qwen3.5-4B 在 1M 上下文下将记忆状态缓存减少 1313$\times$、预填充延迟降低 6.9$\times$，并将吞吐量提高 3.5$\times$、整体记忆性能提升 +5.77%。最后，MemOnce 零样本泛化到下游表示任务，取得与专用模型相当的结果。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 MemOnce 架构，仅缓存最后一层少量隐藏状态作为紧凑记忆并动态解码回 KV 缓存，配合跨层只计算一次稀疏索引的记忆稀疏注意力，在 1M 上下文下将 Qwen3.5-4B 的记忆状态缓存减少 1313 倍、预填充延迟降低 6.9 倍。

匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pretraining, post-training
evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：extensive experiment

papers.title: Learning When to Ask: Advisor-Aware Post-Training for SLM Agents
papers.abstract_en: Small language models (SLMs) are increasingly attractive for cheap, high-throughput agentic deployment, but they remain weak at multi-step reasoning and tool use that long-horizon tasks demand. We study how to post-train an SLM to seek advice from a stronger model and act on that advice itself, following an advisor-executor pattern. Out of the box, this pattern fails across open- and closed-source small-model families: wiring an SLM to an advisor is a harness-design matter that is not enough on its own. A post-training recipe is needed to teach the model when to ask, in a cost-aware fashion, and how to follow advice across steps. Our method, ADAPT (ADvisor-Aware Post-Training), is a multi-stage recipe that instills this behavior, learning entirely from the policy's own rollouts supervised by the environment's outcome, with no learned reward model or human annotation. Across three domains, compared to an untrained harness baseline, ADAPT improves success rate in embodied text reasoning (TextWorld) from 24.5% to 77.3%, code generation (LiveCodeBench) from 21.8% to 56.0%, and deep web search (GAIA) from 17.5% to 49.3%, while querying the advisor sparingly (~1.0-2.1 calls per task). On the two long-horizon domains it closes 70-85% of the gap to an oracle that perfectly times when to ask for advice, and on code generation it exceeds that oracle. The gains persist when the advisor is replaced by one unseen in training, showing that the learned help-seeking policy is robust to a changing advisor rather than tied to the one it was trained with.
papers.abstract_zh: 小语言模型（SLM）因低成本、高吞吐的智能体部署而日益受到青睐，但它们在长时程任务所需的多步推理和工具使用方面仍然较弱。我们研究如何对 SLM 进行后训练，使其向更强模型寻求建议并自行依据建议行动，遵循顾问-执行者模式。开箱即用情况下，该模式在开源和闭源小模型系列上均失败：将 SLM 接入顾问属于框架设计问题，仅此本身并不足够。需要一种后训练方案来教会模型以成本感知的方式何时提问，以及如何跨步骤遵循建议。我们的方法 ADAPT（ADvisor-Aware Post-Training）是一种多阶段方案，用于灌输该行为，完全从策略自身的 rollout 中学习，由环境结果监督，无需学习奖励模型或人工标注。在三个领域中，与未训练的框架基线相比，ADAPT 将具身文本推理（TextWorld）的成功率从 24.5% 提升至 77.3%，代码生成（LiveCodeBench）从 21.8% 提升至 56.0%，深度网络搜索（GAIA）从 17.5% 提升至 49.3%，同时仅少量查询顾问（每任务约 1.0-2.1 次调用）。在两个长时程领域，它缩小了与完美把握提问时机的 oracle 之间 70-85% 的差距，在代码生成上则超过该 oracle。当顾问被替换为训练中未见过的模型时增益仍然保持，表明学到的求助策略对变化的顾问具有鲁棒性，而非绑定于训练时的顾问。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 ADAPT 多阶段后训练方案，仅用策略自身 rollout 和环境结果监督教会 SLM 成本感知地向更强顾问求助并遵循建议，在 TextWorld、LiveCodeBench 和 GAIA 上将成功率分别从 24.5%、21.8%、17.5% 提升至 77.3%、56.0%、49.3%。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training

papers.title: Beyond a Single Human Demonstration: Learning from Scored Trajectory Alternatives for End-to-End Driving
papers.abstract_en: Human driving logs record only one trajectory per scene, leaving other feasible driving choices without explicit trajectory targets or quality labels. This limits supervision for end-to-end planners that generate and refine multiple candidate trajectories. Meanwhile, conditioning refinement on a large vision-language model adds substantial online inference cost. We propose DriveSTA, which extends autoregressive proposal generation and proposal-conditioned residual flow refinement with scored trajectory alternatives. For each training scene, we generate alternatives offline through smooth deformations of the recorded trajectory and evaluate their simulated execution against logged traffic. Diverse, high-quality alternatives supervise distinct proposals and define residual targets for quality-guided denoising, while candidates spanning the full score range train a scorer to assess driving quality. A shared joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), adapted through masked video-feature prediction, encodes observed frames once and provides temporal context for both refinement and scoring. On NAVSIM v1 Navtest, DriveSTA ranks first among the compared planners trained on NAVSIM data alone. With expanded training data, DriveSTA-Scale achieves state-of-the-art results among the compared methods on Navtest and closed-loop HUGSIM, while reducing mean planner forward-pass latency by 73% relative to ChainFlow-VLA in matched evaluations.
papers.abstract_zh: 人类驾驶日志每个场景仅记录一条轨迹，使其他可行驾驶选择缺乏显式轨迹目标或质量标签。这限制了对生成并精炼多条候选轨迹的端到端规划器的监督。同时，以大型视觉语言模型为条件进行精炼会增加大量在线推理成本。我们提出 DriveSTA，以带评分的轨迹替代方案扩展自回归提案生成和以提案为条件的残差流精炼。对于每个训练场景，我们通过记录轨迹的平滑变形离线生成替代方案，并针对记录的交通评估其模拟执行。多样、高质量的替代方案监督不同的提案，并为质量引导的去噪定义残差目标，而覆盖完整分数范围的候选训练评分器以评估驾驶质量。一个共享的联合嵌入预测架构（JEPA）经掩码视频特征预测适配，一次编码观测帧，并为精炼和评分提供时间上下文。在 NAVSIM v1 Navtest 上，DriveSTA 在仅用 NAVSIM 数据训练的对比规划器中排名第一。在扩展训练数据后，DriveSTA-Scale 在 Navtest 和闭环 HUGSIM 上于对比方法中取得最先进结果，同时在匹配评估中将平均规划器前向传播延迟相对 ChainFlow-VLA 降低 73%。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 DriveSTA，通过记录轨迹的平滑变形离线生成带评分的轨迹替代方案，用于监督自回归提案生成与残差流精炼并训练评分器，在 NAVSIM v1 Navtest 上于仅用 NAVSIM 数据训练的规划器中排名第一，且前向延迟较 ChainFlow-VLA 降低 73%。
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Potential emergence in LLM agents: a statistical physics perspective
papers.abstract_en: There has been significant recent interest in understanding the behaviour of LLM agents from the perspective of human preferences or corpus statistics. In this paper we propose agent states as intermediate variables through which post-training can be measured and predicted. From a statistical physics perspective, we study the emergence of a global potential which governs the transition of state in LLM agent reasoning. We introduce a partition function to model the ideal KL-regularised transition distribution and track potential structure, mean reward and state entropy. We demonstrate our approach in two Qwen3.5-9B tasks: safety-test selection and physics-reasoning auditing. We observe that the potential structure strengthens during post-training as predicted from our framework, while joint changes in reward and state entropy provide consistency evidence. States thus provide a quantitative description of how post-training organises agent behaviour.
papers.abstract_zh: 近期有大量研究兴趣从人类偏好或语料统计的角度理解 LLM 智能体的行为。本文提出智能体状态作为中间变量，通过其可测量和预测后训练。我们从统计物理视角研究支配 LLM 智能体推理中状态转移的全局势函数的涌现。我们引入配分函数来建模理想的 KL 正则化转移分布，并追踪势结构、平均奖励和状态熵。我们在两个 Qwen3.5-9B 任务上演示该方法：安全测试选择和物理推理审计。我们观察到，如框架所预测，势结构在后训练期间增强，而奖励和状态熵的联合变化提供了一致性证据。因此，状态为后训练如何组织智能体行为提供了定量描述。
papers.tldr_zh: 从统计物理视角提出以智能体状态为中间变量，用配分函数建模 KL 正则化转移分布并追踪势结构、平均奖励和状态熵，在 Qwen3.5-9B 的安全测试选择与物理推理审计任务上观察到势结构在后训练期间增强。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Can Vision-Language Models Synthesize Executable Game-Playing Programs?
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in vision-language models (VLMs) have endowed multimodal agents with increasingly strong visual perception and long-horizon reasoning capabilities, making VLM-based autonomous game playing feasible. Existing game benchmarks primarily evaluate whether an agent can select appropriate actions from the current visual state across different scenarios and games. However, most of them adopt a step-by-step interaction paradigm where the current visual observation is sent to the agent before each action. In practical deployment, this paradigm introduces two fundamental limitations: the game loop must wait for model inference, making real-time interaction impractical, and repeated VLM calls incur substantial cost. Therefore, we propose PlayScriptBench, a script-based game benchmark that evaluates whether VLMs can synthesize an executable game-playing program from game states. This setting jointly evaluates visual grounding, understanding of game dynamics, long-horizon strategic reasoning, and executable program synthesis, providing a more comprehensive assessment of game-playing agents. To support more tractable evaluation for current general-purpose VLMs, we further introduce a four-stage pipeline --- Explore, Perception, API Construction, and Strategy Composition --- that decomposes controller synthesis into game exploration, state perception, interface construction, and strategic control, enabling agents to progressively construct an executable program. Experiments on 16 games spanning 4 genres show that even strong VLMs struggle on our benchmark, revealing a substantial gap between passive visual game understanding and executable closed-loop game control. These results establish script-based controller synthesis as a complementary direction for benchmarking VLM-based game-playing agents.
papers.abstract_zh: 近期视觉语言模型（VLM）的进展使多模态智能体具备了越来越强的视觉感知与长程推理能力，使得基于 VLM 的自主游戏游玩成为可能。现有游戏基准主要评估智能体能否在不同场景和游戏中根据当前视觉状态选择合适动作。然而，它们大多采用逐步交互范式，即在每次动作前将当前视觉观察发送给智能体。在实际部署中，该范式带来两个根本性限制：游戏循环必须等待模型推理，使实时交互不可行；重复调用 VLM 带来可观成本。因此，我们提出 PlayScriptBench，一个基于脚本的游戏基准，评估 VLM 能否从游戏状态合成可执行的游戏游玩程序。该设定联合评估视觉定位、对游戏动态的理解、长程策略推理以及可执行程序合成，从而对游戏智能体进行更全面的评估。为对当前通用 VLM 支持更可行的评估，我们进一步引入四阶段流水线——探索、感知、API 构建与策略组合——将控制器合成分解为游戏探索、状态感知、接口构建与策略控制，使智能体能够逐步构建可执行程序。在涵盖 4 个类型的 16 款游戏上的实验表明，即便是强 VLM 在我们的基准上也表现吃力，揭示了被动视觉游戏理解与可执行闭环游戏控制之间的显著差距。这些结果确立了基于脚本的控制器合成作为评估基于 VLM 的游戏智能体的一个互补方向。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出基于脚本的游戏基准 PlayScriptBench，要求 VLM 从游戏状态合成可执行游玩程序，并设计探索、感知、API 构建、策略组合四阶段流水线，在 16 款游戏上发现强 VLM 仍难以完成闭环可执行控制。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language model (VLM)-based agents offer a promising approach to robotic manipulation, yet remain limited by inadequate memory organization, uncertain failure attribution, and limited reuse of execution experience. We propose Embodied-Harness, a dual-agent framework that improves manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model parameters. The Actor interacts with the environment through a robot-control interface, while the Reflector converts execution evidence into reusable operational guidance. Hierarchical Memory Architecture maintains short-term execution context and long-term experiential knowledge to support execution and reflection. Evidence-based Experience Reflection grounds failure diagnosis in observed interactions, while Recursive Harness Self-Improvement refines operational guidance across successive attempts. Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboSPA, and RMBench demonstrate the effectiveness of Embodied-Harness in generalization under environmental variations, spatial reasoning, long-horizon planning, and memory-dependent manipulation. Our method achieves success rates of 82.4%, 76.7%, and 94.4% on the three benchmarks, respectively. Real-world evaluation further yields an average success rate of 96.7% across three manipulation tasks. These results highlight the potential of Embodied-Harness to improve robotic manipulation through experience-driven harness self-improvement.
papers.abstract_zh: 基于视觉语言模型（VLM）的智能体为机器人操作提供了有前景的途径，但仍受限于记忆组织不足、失败归因不确定以及执行经验复用有限。我们提出 Embodied-Harness，一个双智能体框架，通过改进执行 harness 而不更新模型参数来提升操作能力。Actor 通过机器人控制接口与环境交互，Reflector 将执行证据转化为可复用的操作指导。分层记忆架构维护短期执行上下文与长期经验知识，以支持执行与反思。基于证据的经验反思将失败诊断建立在观测到的交互之上，而递归 Harness 自我改进在连续尝试中改进操作指导。在 RoboTwin 2.0、RoboSPA 和 RMBench 上的实验证明了 Embodied-Harness 在环境变化下的泛化、空间推理、长程规划以及依赖记忆的操作方面的有效性。我们的方法在三个基准上分别达到 82.4%、76.7% 和 94.4% 的成功率。真实世界评估在三个操作任务上进一步取得平均 96.7% 的成功率。这些结果凸显了 Embodied-Harness 通过经验驱动的 harness 自我改进来提升机器人操作的潜力。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出双智能体框架 Embodied-Harness，由 Actor 执行、Reflector 反思，结合分层记忆与递归 harness 自我改进，在不更新模型参数下于三个基准取得 82.4%、76.7%、94.4% 成功率，真实任务平均 96.7%。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: SOAR: Training-Free Rank-Consistent Rollout Compression for Latent World Model Planning
papers.abstract_en: Latent world models plan by rolling out hundreds of candidate action sequences through a transformer predictor, so a single decision can take tens of seconds. Existing accelerations prune spatial tokens as in vision-language models, yet a sampling-based planner uses predicted costs only to rank candidates, so a rollout can be compressed freely as long as the ranking survives. We propose SOAR, a training-free method that adapts rollout compression to each planning decision. At every decision, SOAR probes a few candidates under several token budgets and keeps the smallest budget that preserves their ranking, so it compresses as far as the current decision allows, without task labels. A closed-loop study of more than 80,000 episodes fixes the rest of the rollout: the first step, which alone reads a real observation, stays exact, and the context frame is cached rather than recomputed. On seven navigation and manipulation tasks with frozen checkpoints, SOAR matches dense-level planning success at 2.3x speedup and retains 98% at 2.5x. Our code is available at https://github.com/starrywiki/SOAR.
papers.abstract_zh: 潜在世界模型通过 transformer 预测器对数百个候选动作序列进行 rollout 来规划，因此单次决策可能耗时数十秒。现有加速方法如视觉语言模型那样剪枝空间 token，然而基于采样的规划器仅使用预测代价对候选进行排序，因此只要排序得以保留，rollout 就可以自由压缩。我们提出 SOAR，一种无需训练的方法，针对每个规划决策自适应地压缩 rollout。在每个决策处，SOAR 在若干 token 预算下探测少量候选，并保留能维持其排序的最小预算，从而在当前决策允许的范围内尽可能压缩，且无需任务标签。对超过 80,000 个回合的闭环研究固定了 rollout 的其余部分：第一步（唯一读取真实观测的步骤）保持精确，上下文帧被缓存而非重新计算。在七个导航与操作任务上使用冻结检查点，SOAR 在 2.3 倍加速下达到与稠密级规划相当的成功率，在 2.5 倍加速下保持 98%。我们的代码见 https://github.com/starrywiki/SOAR。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出免训练方法 SOAR，在每个规划决策处探测候选在不同 token 预算下的排序并保留维持排序的最小预算，配合首步精确与上下文缓存，在七个任务上以 2.3 倍加速达到稠密级成功率、2.5 倍加速保持 98%。

papers.title: Functional Depth Is Learned: Isolating the Computation That Layers Produce Only Together
papers.abstract_en: Transformer performance scales with depth, but layer count merely counts the opportunities for sequential computation: layers could still behave as nearly independent refinements that barely depend on one another. We study how transformers develop functional depth during pretraining, introducing an exact inclusion-exclusion decomposition that isolates the connected component, i.e., the computation that appears only when a specified set of layers acts together under identity ablation. Tracking this quantity across public checkpoints of Pythia, OLMo, and Amber yields three findings. First, write-relative connected coordination strengthens from its initialization or earliest-checkpoint baseline as pretraining proceeds, across all measured interaction orders. Second, these connected components are behaviorally consequential under direct intervention: deleting them damages perplexity more than deleting a norm-matched random direction at the same site in all 35 measured model-order cells. Third, pairwise representation similarity is consistently negatively correlated with pairwise connected coordination across seven models, yet the two signals are not interchangeable: similarity- and coordination-based block-removal criteria often agree in Pythia but diverge on Amber. Together, these results suggest that architectural depth provides the opportunity for sequential computation, while pretraining progressively organizes cross-layer dependencies within that depth.
papers.abstract_zh: Transformer 的性能随深度扩展，但层数仅计入了顺序计算的机会：各层仍可能表现为几乎独立、彼此依赖甚微的细化。我们研究 transformer 在预训练中如何发展出功能深度，引入精确的容斥分解，以在恒等消融下隔离连通分量，即仅当指定层集合共同作用时才出现的计算。在 Pythia、OLMo 和 Amber 的公开检查点上追踪该量，得到三点发现。第一，随预训练推进，写相对连通协调从初始化或最早检查点基线起增强，且覆盖所有测量的交互阶数。第二，这些连通分量在直接干预下具有行为后果：在所有 35 个测量的模型-阶数单元中，删除它们对困惑度的损害均大于在同一位置删除范数匹配的随机方向。第三，在七个模型上，成对表示相似度与成对连通协调持续负相关，但两种信号不可互换：基于相似度与基于协调的块移除准则在 Pythia 上常一致，但在 Amber 上出现分歧。综上，这些结果表明架构深度为顺序计算提供了机会，而预训练在该深度内逐步组织跨层依赖。
papers.tldr_zh: 引入精确容斥分解隔离仅当多层共同作用时才出现的连通计算，在 Pythia、OLMo、Amber 检查点上发现预训练逐步增强跨层连通协调，且该分量在干预下对困惑度影响大于范数匹配随机方向。

papers.title: $\varepsilon$-SegFormer: Multi-Resolution Vision Transformers for Sparsely Supervised Segmentation in Electron Microscopy
papers.abstract_en: Segmenting organelles in electron microscopy (EM) volumes requires dense annotations that take experts months to produce, and every gain in imaging resolution adds to this cost. Sparsely supervised methods reduce this cost to a small fraction of labeled pixels, but the convolutional networks they build on see a limited neighborhood around each pixel, while the identity of an organelle often depends on context far beyond it. We introduce $\varepsilon$-SegFormer, a multi-resolution Vision Transformer for sparsely supervised semantic segmentation, which builds on the architecture of MuViT and extends the training method of $\varepsilon$-Seg. For each labeled pixel, $\varepsilon$-SegFormer samples views at three physical resolutions centered on it, embeds their patches into a single token sequence, and encodes every token's position in image coordinates, so that attention relates all views in one shared frame. A segmentation head classifies the pixel from the tokens around it; during training, the pixel's own token is hidden, so the label must be predicted from context rather than local appearance. The model is trained in a single stage, without pretraining, with an auxiliary reconstruction loss. On the BetaSeg FIB-SEM dataset, $\varepsilon$-SegFormer learns from about 10,000 labeled pixels among the 670 million voxels inside three cells, and, given the cell mask, segments nuclei, mitochondria and insulin granules in a slice of a fourth, unseen cell with an average Dice of 0.89 (0.91 after post-processing). Ablations show that coarser views improve accuracy and that a compact head on local tokens works best, with the wider context entering through attention in the encoder.
papers.abstract_zh: 在电子显微镜（EM）体积中分割细胞器需要专家耗时数月制作的稠密标注，而成像分辨率的每一次提升都会增加这一成本。稀疏监督方法将成本降至少量标注像素，但其基于的卷积网络只能看到每个像素周围的有限邻域，而细胞器的身份往往取决于远超该邻域的上下文。我们提出 ε-SegFormer，一种用于稀疏监督语义分割的多分辨率 Vision Transformer，基于 MuViT 的架构并扩展 ε-Seg 的训练方法。对于每个标注像素，ε-SegFormer 以其为中心在三种物理分辨率下采样视图，将其 patch 嵌入单一 token 序列，并编码每个 token 在图像坐标中的位置，使注意力在共享帧中关联所有视图。分割头根据周围 token 对该像素分类；训练时该像素自身的 token 被隐藏，因此标签必须从上下文而非局部外观预测。模型单阶段训练，无需预训练，并带有辅助重建损失。在 BetaSeg FIB-SEM 数据集上，ε-SegFormer 从三个细胞内 6.7 亿体素中的约 10,000 个标注像素学习，并在给定细胞掩码的情况下，在第四个未见细胞的切片中分割细胞核、线粒体和胰岛素颗粒，平均 Dice 为 0.89（后处理后 0.91）。消融表明更粗的视图提升准确率，且局部 token 上的紧凑头效果最佳，更广的上下文通过编码器中的注意力进入。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出多分辨率 Vision Transformer ε-SegFormer，对每个标注像素采样三种物理分辨率视图并隐藏自身 token 以强制上下文预测，在 BetaSeg FIB-SEM 上仅用约 1 万标注像素于未见细胞切片取得平均 Dice 0.89。

papers.title: From Manufacturing Event Logs to Simulation: Enabling SMEs with Agentic AI for SimPy Simulation Generation
papers.abstract_en: High expertise and cost barriers exclude small and medium-sized enterprises from discrete-event simulation (DES). We introduce GenAI4SimPy, a multi-agent framework powered by Qwen 3.6 (27B), an open-weight large language model, that automates end-to-end DES generation from manufacturing event logs to executable SimPy models through tool-augmented reasoning and human-in-the-loop validation. Evaluated on three execution blocks from a public smart factory dataset, the framework achieved a mean absolute percentage error of 7.9\% and coverage of failure rate for all three blocks and of throughput for two of three. A fidelity paradox was observed: accurate process-level parameters did not ensure system-level behavioral fidelity, with flow-time and throughput errors driven by misinterpreted observation-window truncation and absent system-level calibration. These results demonstrate that local open-weight models can perform DES generation at accuracy comparable to cloud-based alternatives, while identifying parameter extraction as necessary but insufficient for behavioral validity. Source code and results are available at https://github.com/RaikoPipe/genai4simpy
papers.abstract_zh: 高专业知识和成本壁垒使中小企业无法使用离散事件仿真（DES）。我们提出 GenAI4SimPy，一个由开放权重大语言模型 Qwen 3.6（27B）驱动的多智能体框架，通过工具增强推理和人在回路验证，自动化从制造事件日志到可执行 SimPy 模型的端到端 DES 生成。在公共智能工厂数据集的三个执行块上评估，该框架实现了 7.9% 的平均绝对百分比误差，并在全部三个执行块上覆盖了故障率、在三个执行块中的两个上覆盖了吞吐量。观察到保真度悖论：准确的流程级参数并不能保证系统级行为保真度，流动时间和吞吐量误差源于对观察窗口截断的误解释以及缺乏系统级校准。这些结果表明，本地开放权重模型能够以与云端替代方案相当的精度执行 DES 生成，同时指出参数提取对于行为有效性是必要但不充分的。源代码和结果见 https://github.com/RaikoPipe/genai4simpy。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出基于 Qwen 3.6（27B）的多智能体框架 GenAI4SimPy，从制造事件日志自动生成可执行 SimPy 仿真模型，在公共智能工厂数据集三个执行块上取得 7.9% 平均绝对百分比误差，并发现流程级参数准确不足以保障系统级行为保真度。

papers.title: When Visually Rich Documents Meet Multi-Vector Retrieval for Region-level Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.abstract_en: Visually rich documents (VRDs) convey knowledge through textual, visual, and layout information that text-centric Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Text-RAG) struggles to fully exploit. Recent Vision-RAG approaches enable retrieval and generation directly from document images, retaining this multimodal information. However, earlier Vision-RAG methods commonly adopt coarse retrieval representations and full-page visual contexts, which can obscure local evidence and introduce substantial redundancy and computational overhead. To address these challenges, we propose MV-VisRAG, a region-level Vision-RAG framework that uses semantically complete regions for both document representation and visual augmentation. Specifically, MV-VisRAG first constructs these regions through a ContentAdaptive Regionalization module. It then encodes them into local region vectors and a page-level global vector using a VLM-based retriever trained through multimodal reconstruction pretraining and retrieval fine-tuning. With this compact multi-vector representation, MV-VisRAG performs late-interaction retrieval and estimates region contributions from the resulting matching scores. These contributions guide the selection of relevant regions, which are then rearranged into a compact visual context for generation. Experiments across five benchmarks demonstrate retrieval and generation gains over corresponding baselines, while region-level augmentation substantially reduces visual tokens and computational cost. Our code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/xandery-geek/MV-VisRAG.
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉丰富文档（VRD）通过文本、视觉和布局信息传达知识，而以文本为中心的检索增强生成（Text-RAG）难以充分利用这些信息。近期的 Vision-RAG 方法能够直接从文档图像进行检索和生成，保留这种多模态信息。然而，早期 Vision-RAG 方法通常采用粗粒度检索表示和整页视觉上下文，这可能掩盖局部证据并引入大量冗余和计算开销。为应对这些挑战，我们提出 MV-VisRAG，一个区域级 Vision-RAG 框架，使用语义完整的区域进行文档表示和视觉增强。具体而言，MV-VisRAG 首先通过内容自适应区域化模块构建这些区域，然后使用经多模态重建预训练和检索微调的基于 VLM 的检索器，将它们编码为局部区域向量和页面级全局向量。借助这种紧凑的多向量表示，MV-VisRAG 执行后期交互检索，并根据匹配分数估计区域贡献。这些贡献指导相关区域的选择，随后被重新排列为紧凑的视觉上下文用于生成。在五个基准上的实验表明，相对于相应基线在检索和生成上均有提升，同时区域级增强大幅减少了视觉 token 和计算成本。代码将公开于 https://github.com/xandery-geek/MV-VisRAG。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出区域级 Vision-RAG 框架 MV-VisRAG，用语义完整区域构建局部与页面级多向量表示并进行后期交互检索，在五个基准上提升检索与生成效果并降低视觉 token 与计算成本。

papers.title: PhiJEPA: Denoising Latent Predictions for Visual Representation Learning
papers.abstract_en: Can a predictor trained to infer hidden image regions still help a world model plan when part of an object disappears from view and the visible context is blurred? We introduce PhiJEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architecture that adapts PhiNet's two-stage prediction to masked Transformers. From sparse, photometrically corrupted context, a Transformer block predicts hidden tokens of an independently corrupted teacher view. A token-wise MLP then maps these predictions to clean teacher tokens. Controlled ablations show that the combined objective improves dense features over the tested one-stage alternatives. Pre-trained on ImageNet-1K with $5.6\times10^{19}$ training FLOPs, PhiJEPA achieves 69.3 mIoU on linear PASCAL VOC segmentation, exceeding the evaluated I-JEPA and DSeq-JEPA checkpoints in segmentation accuracy, with 25\% fewer training FLOPs than I-JEPA. It also improves hidden-region segmentation over Simple I-JEPA (49.1 vs.\ 44.3 mIoU). As an application, we use the frozen encoder in DINO-WM on PushT, and reuse the pre-training predictor, which JEPAs usually discard, to complete occluded tokens without fine-tuning. In open-loop planning with simultaneous object occlusion and Gaussian blur ($σ=2$ pixels), predictor completion raises success from 33\% to 65\%, compared with 25\% for Simple I-JEPA with its predictor and 40\% for iBOT with pixel inpainting. Together, these results support two-stage latent prediction as an efficient approach to learning visual representations that remain useful under photometric degradation and support completion under partial observation.
papers.abstract_zh: 一个被训练用于推断隐藏图像区域的预测器，当物体的一部分从视野中消失且可见上下文模糊时，是否仍能帮助世界模型进行规划？我们提出 PhiJEPA，一种联合嵌入预测架构，将 PhiNet 的两阶段预测适配到掩码 Transformer。从稀疏、光度损坏的上下文出发，一个 Transformer 块预测独立损坏的教师视图的隐藏 token。随后一个逐 token MLP 将这些预测映射到干净的教师 token。受控消融表明，组合目标相比所测试的单阶段替代方案改善了稠密特征。在 ImageNet-1K 上以 5.6×10^19 训练 FLOPs 预训练后，PhiJEPA 在线性 PASCAL VOC 分割上达到 69.3 mIoU，在分割精度上超过所评估的 I-JEPA 和 DSeq-JEPA 检查点，且训练 FLOPs 比 I-JEPA 少 25%。它还在隐藏区域分割上优于 Simple I-JEPA（49.1 对 44.3 mIoU）。作为应用，我们在 PushT 上将冻结编码器用于 DINO-WM，并复用预训练预测器（JEPAs 通常丢弃）在无需微调的情况下补全被遮挡 token。在同时存在物体遮挡和高斯模糊（σ=2 像素）的开环规划中，预测器补全将成功率从 33% 提升到 65%，相比之下 Simple I-JEPA 使用其预测器为 25%，iBOT 使用像素修复为 40%。这些结果共同支持两阶段潜在预测作为一种高效方法，学习在光度退化下仍然有用并支持部分观测下补全的视觉表示。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出两阶段联合嵌入预测架构 PhiJEPA，在 ImageNet-1K 上预训练后线性 PASCAL VOC 分割达 69.3 mIoU，并复用预训练预测器补全遮挡 token，使 DINO-WM 在遮挡加高斯模糊的开环规划成功率从 33% 提升至 65%。

papers.title: Automating Multi-View Quality Assessment of 3D Annotation Layouts
papers.abstract_en: Text labels provide descriptive information about elements in visual scenes. In 3D visualization, the arrangement of these labels and their connections to target locations forms an annotation layout. Assessing layout quality supports comparisons between alternative layouts. However, existing quality measures often focus on specific layout properties and may not fully reflect human judgments of overall quality. Moreover, a layout may appear clear from one viewpoint but suffer from occlusion or clutter from another. To address these issues, we propose a multi-view quality assessment method based on a multimodal large language model (MLLM). We fine-tune a compact MLLM using structured supervision from human ratings to predict a rating for each quality dimension in each view. These ratings are aggregated into view-level and sample-level quality scores. To support training and evaluation, we construct the Annotation Layouts with Quality Assessment (ALQA) dataset, containing 3,216 layout samples from 1,072 3D objects across 13 categories. Each layout is rendered from 5 predefined viewpoints, and each view is independently rated by 3 human raters across 5 quality dimensions. On ALQA, our method agrees more closely with human reference scores than the evaluated MLLM baselines, and a user study demonstrates strong agreement with human preferences in layout ranking.
papers.abstract_zh: 文本标签提供视觉场景中元素的描述性信息。在 3D 可视化中，这些标签的排列及其与目标位置的连接构成标注布局。评估布局质量有助于比较不同布局方案。然而，现有质量度量通常关注特定布局属性，可能无法充分反映人类对整体质量的判断。此外，布局从一个视角看可能清晰，但从另一视角看可能遭受遮挡或杂乱。为解决这些问题，我们提出一种基于多模态大语言模型（MLLM）的多视角质量评估方法。我们使用来自人类评分的结构化监督微调一个紧凑 MLLM，以预测每个视角中每个质量维度的评分。这些评分被聚合为视角级和样本级质量分数。为支持训练和评估，我们构建了带质量评估的标注布局（ALQA）数据集，包含来自 13 个类别的 1,072 个 3D 对象的 3,216 个布局样本。每个布局从 5 个预定义视角渲染，每个视角由 3 名人类评分者在 5 个质量维度上独立评分。在 ALQA 上，我们的方法比所评估的 MLLM 基线更接近人类参考分数，用户研究也表明在布局排序上与人类偏好高度一致。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出基于微调紧凑多模态大语言模型的多视角 3D 标注布局质量评估方法，并构建含 3,216 个布局样本、5 视角与 5 质量维度的 ALQA 数据集，在评分一致性和布局排序上优于所评估的 MLLM 基线。

匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model

papers.title: Efficient VLA Reinforcement Learning via Subchunk Rollouts in Latent World Models
papers.abstract_en: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) can improve pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policies through imagined experiences. However, existing VLA-MBRL methods primarily rely on large-scale image or video generation world models, incurring large computational overhead. Latent world models offer a more efficient alternative but face two challenges: compounding errors during recursive prediction and incompatibility with VLAs' visual input interfaces. In this work, we propose LS-MBPO, a lightweight residual MBRL framework that leverages latent world models to improve upon pretrained VLAs. LS-MBPO introduces two key techniques: (1) Hierarchical Forcing, which combines dense causal supervision with autoregressive feedback to mitigate compounding prediction errors; and (2) Latent Subchunk Rollouts, which leverage action chunks from a frozen VLA policy and a latent residual policy for successive subchunk refinement, bridging the gap between latent imagination and VLA policy execution. We further introduce a Progress-Conditioned Branch-Start Curriculum that progressively shifts rollout starting points from later to earlier task stages, enabling effective policy learning from short imagined rollouts. Extensive experiments on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and a real-world ALOHA robot show that LS-MBPO achieves superior task performance and training efficiency compared to existing methods.

papers.title: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong semantic understanding but remain limited in their ability to reason about metric 3D space in the physical world. Existing VLMs typically infer 3D scene structure from one or more images without known camera calibration or cross-view geometric constraints. This makes metric 3D inference inherently ambiguous and leaves it unclear whether their spatial predictions are grounded in visual evidence or driven primarily by semantic priors. In contrast, calibrated stereo provides explicit cross-view geometry that resolves this ambiguity and offers a more reliable foundation for metric 3D perception and geometric generalization. We investigate how VLMs can learn transferable 3D representations directly from calibrated binocular observations. To this end, we introduce StereoVLM, the first geometry-aware binocular VLM for metric 3D spatial reasoning. StereoVLM follows a hierarchical learning paradigm spanning from cross-view correspondence and disparity estimation to calibration-conditioned metric depth perception and semantic spatial reasoning. We further find that disparity supervision generalizes substantially better than direct binocular depth supervision on unseen environments. To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce Stereo3D-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark across three levels, from point-level geometry to object-level spatial reasoning. StereoVLM-8B achieves 95.17% depth accuracy ($δ_1$) and a 66.98 average object-level score on Stereo3D-Bench. Intervention results further indicate that the model's performance on Stereo3D-Bench benefits from valid cross-view geometry and cannot be explained solely by additional visual tokens or semantic priors. Hierarchical geometric supervision also yields average gains of 3.54 points across five spatial benchmarks and 4.3 percentage points in RoboCasa manipulation success.

papers.title: RoSci: Exploring Robustness in Science VLMs
papers.abstract_en: Recent advancements in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) enable significant progress in scientific tasks. However, these models are generally assumed to be presented with complete and accurate information, overlooking the challenges of erroneous/missing information in wild scenarios. To address this gap, we introduce the concept of Scientific Model Robustness, which defines a model's ability to detect anomalies, assess solvability, and perform self-calibration when faced with Information Error (inconsistencies) or Information Loss (insufficiency). Specifically, we present RoSci-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark of 1,220 samples using a seed-variant strategy across six degradation types. To address VLM fragility, we further propose RoSci-Agent, a framework that employs a Parse-Verify-Decide pipeline to vet premises before reasoning. The evaluated VLMs sometimes answer questions whose premises are invalid or incomplete. RoSci-Agent achieves a higher Overall Robustness Score than the evaluated standalone VLMs. RoSci-Bench gives the multimodal reasoning community a common test of when models answer, request clarification, or reject a scientific question.

papers.title: Can pretrained Transformers deliver semiparametrically efficient inference?
papers.abstract_en: Semiparametric models provide a broad framework for statistical inference, yet efficient estimation typically relies on influence function correction tailored to each estimand and on nuisance estimation repeated for every sample. We show that a single pretrained Transformer can deliver efficient estimation and valid inference for a family of estimands in one forward pass, without deriving efficient influence functions or estimating nuisance functions. Pretrained on simulated data with the true parameter as the only label, the Transformer learns the posterior mean and covariance of the queried estimand and hence returns an estimate and a Wald-type confidence region. Theoretically, we prove that, for locally flat pretraining priors of slowly growing complexity, the posterior mean is efficient for every queried estimand. The Transformer inherits this efficiency with asymptotically exact coverage, in probability over evaluation populations and queries, even under distribution shift. We also reveal that the guarantee places much higher demands on pretraining when the data-generating distribution is fixed, as in classical frequentist inference. Experiments on causal inference, partial linear regression, and survival analysis show that the pretrained model generally achieves the lowest estimation error among competing methods, with nearly nominal coverage, at a computational cost of only about 0.02 seconds per dataset.

papers.title: Seeing Is Not Steering: Where Verifiable Reasoning Can Enter an End-to-End Driving Planner
papers.abstract_en: Driving models that reason may describe a hazard correctly while choosing their path for other reasons. We study where scene reasoning can enter an end-to-end planner so its influence can be checked. We freeze Drive-JEPA and use a fine-tuned vision-language model to state scene facts. Although fine-tuning improves fact accuracy, the two learned components we test show no detectable benefit from reading them. A rule-based fact check instead rejects or shortens paths that contradict the facts, linking each intervention to a stated fact. On the frozen planner alone, it gains 2.4 EPDMS points on navhard. Its 2.0-point margin over a control that changes the same frames without consulting facts remains statistically uncertain. A diagnostic using exact facts from maps and annotations yields a 3.6-point margin over its corresponding control, with a 95% confidence interval above zero. Separately, a path scorer and plan memory that read no stated facts raise navhard from 41.2 to 51.8. Bounding travel distance using the reasoner's facts adds 0.3 there and reduces navtest by 2.0. The fact check makes each intervention auditable, while the driving value of the reasoner's facts remains unresolved.

papers.title: Auditing Post-Training Unlearning in Diffusion Language Models using Sparse Autoencoders
papers.abstract_en: Machine unlearning is an approach to privacy protection: it aims to remove the influence of designated data while preserving the model's behavior on information that should be retained. While a growing body of work investigates this objective in autoregressive large language models, machine unlearning remains underexplored in diffusion language models (DLMs). DLMs generate text through iterative denoising, exposing partially masked states whose internal representations change throughout the generation process. This raises a DLM-specific question: can selective forgetting improve by identifying forget-data-associated features and adapting their suppression across denoising stages? We conduct a controlled investigation of this question in LLaDA-8B-Instruct. To evaluate the unlearning of knowledge plausibly encoded during pre-training, we use WMDP as our forget-domain benchmark. Using top-k sparse autoencoders and denoising-state replay, we compare static and stage-adaptive feature suppression. We find substantial shifts in forget-data-associated features across denoising stages, but tracking these dynamics alone does not reliably improve the forget-retain trade-off at the evaluated operating points. Together, our study provides an initial empirical foundation for developing and evaluating machine unlearning as a post-training privacy mechanism in DLMs.

papers.title: Circular Predictive Coding Unlocks Effective Depth
papers.abstract_en: Predictive coding networks perform credit assignment through an energy minimization process. Despite their ability to train models with arbitrary network topologies, they have mostly been used to train feedforward architectures to match the performance of backpropagation. However, they fail to do so when the models become too deep, because error signals become unstable or vanish as they travel through many layers. We address this limitation with circular networks, which get their depth directly from the energy minimization, rather than from stacking layers. Formally, we prove that convergence to an equilibrium of the energy functional of a circular predictive coding network approximates the fixed-point iteration process of a deep equilibrium model, showing that circularity alone suffices to unlock effective depth. Empirically, we show that circular models (i) outperform other predictive coding models of the same size on image classification tasks, matching the accuracy of state-of-the-art predictive coding ResNets and VGG networks despite having substantially fewer parameters; (ii) solve constraint satisfaction problems that require many steps of iterative reasoning, a task not feasible with feedforward models at all, reaching 99.3% test accuracy on Sudoku-hard via nested energy minimization loops; and (iii) scale to autoregressive language modeling by training a circular transformer on TinyStories and WikiText-103, before out of reach for predictive coding models. These results have direct implications for physical neural networks, where computational depth can be traded for recursion on a fixed-size circuit.

papers.title: Structurally Different, Functionally Persistent: Capability Regions Under Model Optimization
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) capabilities have been associated with localized parameter regions, enabling targeted model editing and intervention. However, it remains unclear whether a region identified before model optimization remains an effective intervention target afterward. We evaluate the functional persistence and parameter overlap of coding capability regions across three instruction-tuned models under quantization, pruning, and LoRA-based adaptation. Although re-extracted regions exhibit substantial parameter reorganization, ablating the original region after optimization eliminates or nearly eliminates coding performance in almost all conditions, while magnitude-matched controls preserve performance. Partition analysis further shows that the shared subset of the original and re-extracted regions accounts for most of the observed ablation effect in the majority of conditions. These results demonstrate that parameter overlap and functional persistence are distinct: capability regions can remain causally effective intervention targets even when their parameter realization changes substantially.

papers.title: QuantStream3D: Geometry-Aligned Low-Bit KV Cache Quantization for Streaming Visual Geometry Transformers
papers.abstract_en: Streaming visual geometry transformers retain historical key-value (KV) states as cross-view geometric memory, but growing caches constrain long-sequence inference. We systematically characterize KV quantization in streaming geometry and uncover two linked challenges: Nonuniform Geometric Sensitivity and Cache-Geometry Mismatch. Quantization sensitivity varies across precision choices and cache locations, while perturbed retrieval changes geometry-head inputs and propagates through subsequent predictions and KV writes. Guided by these findings, we propose QuantStream3D, to our knowledge the first dedicated KV quantization framework for streaming visual geometry transformers. Geometry-Guided Mixed-Precision KV Quantization protects sensitive cross-view evidence, while Geometry-Aligned Quantization-Aware Distillation jointly adapts transformer blocks and geometry heads on student-generated quantized history. Across five benchmarks and two backbones, QuantStream3D achieves near-lossless geometric accuracy in most settings with predominantly 2-bit KV caches, and many configurations surpass unquantized inference. Compared with LLM-oriented KV quantizers, it reduces TUM absolute trajectory error and NeuralRGBD completeness error by up to 57.4% and 69.7%, respectively. Integration with existing native cache-pruning methods further pushes compression while improving reconstruction quality on NeuralRGBD. Our optimized StreamVGGT backend achieves $5.05\times$ physical KV compression and 23.1% lower latency at batch size one. Under a fixed memory budget on the same GPU, it supports $5.4\times$ the maximum batch size and up to $1.67\times$ the peak throughput of unquantized inference. Code and pretrained checkpoints will be made publicly available.

papers.title: AppCon-Bench: Perception and Misperception of Material Appearance in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Identifying the same material across changes in illumination or geometry is a critical ability for robust vision systems. Humans exhibit remarkable material appearance constancy, being able to recognize the intrinsic physical properties of an object's surface material across variations in extrinsic, confounding factors such as the lighting or the shape of such object. Vision-Language Models (VLMs) demonstrate strong performance across a wide range of semantic vision tasks, yet their ability to interpret subtle mid-level perceptual attributes remains less understood. We introduce AppCon-Bench, a benchmark comprising five tasks designed to assess material appearance constancy under controlled variations in geometry and illumination, and evaluate representative VLMs alongside human observers, investigating their ability to maintain consistent material judgments across viewing conditions and experimental contexts. After thorough analysis, we identify several key findings that reveal both similarities and systematic differences between human and VLM material appearance perception, highlighting the value of evaluating perceptual successes and failures beyond overall accuracy and informing areas of improvement for current VLMs.

papers.title: Bringing AI Assistance to the Beznau Nuclear Power Plant: A Hierarchical System of LLM Agents for Reactor Monitoring
papers.abstract_en: Beznau Unit 1 in Switzerland, in operation since 1969, is the most experienced nuclear reactor still running worldwide. Five decades of incremental modernization have left its monitoring systems, alarm logs, variable catalogs, technical specifications and investigation reports in separate silos that were never designed to be queried together. As a result, investigating a core instrumentation anomaly means slow, manual gathering of knowledge scattered across databases, documents, and experienced colleagues. We present a hierarchical multi-agent assistant built on large language models (LLMs) to support these investigations and reduce the need for tedious manual searches in SAP systems. An orchestrating agent breaks down an engineer's question and hands the parts to specialized sub-agents, each with read-only access to one source. Domain expertise is written as natural-language procedures that plant engineers can read, review and revise. The system is strictly advisory, with every answer traced back to its sources. We also report organizational lessons from introducing agentic AI into a culture built on safety, traceability and conservative change. Beyond the technical architecture, the Beznau case study examines how an assistant can be introduced into a setting where evidence must be traceable, changes carefully reviewed, and operational decisions retained by plant personnel, paving the way for the responsible use of agentic AI in industrial plant monitoring.

papers.title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
papers.abstract_en: Machine learning has largely kept separate the choice of architecture and the process of training. A classic Transformer, for instance, trains a fixed set of attention and MLP sublayers at every layer, in the same order, and optimizes the weights within. This uniformity is a convention rather than a principled design choice, and it is likely suboptimal: the best architecture for a given task may be smaller, more efficient, and far from uniform. We believe that, ideally, training itself should shape the model's topology. To this end, we introduce Model Carving, which learns both a Transformer's weights and its architecture in a single run. By applying learnable, scalar gates to each sublayer, we allow the training loss to remove the model's own components during training -- freeing a smaller heterogeneous network inside. We evaluate Model Carving by pre-training standard Transformers from 140M to 2.7B parameters and looped Transformers from 140M to 1.3B. At equal training compute, carved models reach a lower validation loss than dense models trained with up to 1.7 times more compute. Furthermore, carved models also outperform size-matched models produced by pruning or distillation, suggesting that the best way to obtain small models for edge devices is to carve them during training, not to compress a large one afterwards. This advantage both grows with scale and carries over to downstream tasks such as few-shot evaluation and generation. Because the removed sublayers no longer run, carved models also cost up to 34% fewer FLOPs per token and decode up to 1.6 times faster without cost in quality. Our results show that architecture, like weights, should be learned and not fixed in advance, and that inside every large transformer is a smaller, faster, stronger one waiting to be carved out.

papers.title: PaMuk-Bench: A Parallel Multilingual Multitask Benchmark for Vision-Language Tasks
papers.abstract_en: While vision-language models (VLMs) currently obtain notable results for highly-studied languages, e.g. English, they exhibit significant performance drops in certain low-resource languages, especially due to the lack of annotated datasets. To this end, we propose PaMuk-Bench, a novel parallel multilingual multitask benchmark for vision-language tasks. Our benchmark includes a set of over 10K curated English prompts that are translated into six languages: Arabic, Danish, French, Hindi, Italian, Romanian. Parallel translations, which are obtained via a semi-automatic process, along with accompanying generated and retrieved images enable the comparative development and evaluation of VLMs across a wide range of tasks: text-to-image generation, image captioning, content-based image retrieval, image generation difficulty estimation, image retrieval difficulty estimation. We empirically show that zero-shot English and multilingual pre-trained VLMs compare consistently worse than their fine-tuned counterparts, confirming that PaMuk-Bench is a valuable resource that can drastically reduce the language gap across a variety of VLM architectures and tasks. PaMuk-Bench is available at https://github.com/ghesil/pamuk_bench.

papers.title: Cannot Wait to Verify: Parallel Drafting to Eliminate Verifier Idle Time in Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract_en: Autoregressive inference in large transformer models is limited by token-level sequential execution, resulting in high latency and low GPU utilization. Speculative decoding (SD) mitigates this bottleneck by introducing a draft-and-verifier model. However, the drafting stage remains sequential, leaving the verifier idle and underutilizing compute. To address this, we propose a plug-and-play drafting adaptive drafting method that parallelizes inference across transformer layers during draft generation. Starting from a shared hidden state, our approach evaluates multiple layers in parallel and verifies consistency by measuring divergence in hidden-state space. Layer-wise draft states are accepted when deviations are small; otherwise, a correction step is applied. By exploiting redundancy across transformer layers, our method accelerates draft generation and improves hardware utilization without modifying architectures or requiring retraining. Experimental results on NLP tasks show that our method speeds up the drafting stage by up to $1.65\times$ with minimal degradation in accuracy, while maintaining the same performance as SD.

papers.title: Alignment without Transfer: Tokenization Impacts Cross-lingual Representations during Multilingual Language Model Pretraining
papers.abstract_en: Tokenization represents one of the most crucial steps in mulilingual NLP pipelines. Yet, tokenizers routinely under-allocate vocabulary to low-resource languages. While improved allocation leads to better performance, it remains poorly understood how tokenization shapes cross-lingual representations and transfer during pretraining. To address this, we pretrain 39 mono- and bilingual 1B decoder-only models on FineWeb2-HQ across English, German, French, Arabic and Chinese, varying only the tokenizer. Our results demonstrate that improved vocabulary allocation (i) substantially raises cross-lingual representation alignment in early-to-mid layers, an effect that prior work measuring only the output layer could not observe, (ii) increases cross-lingual parametric knowledge sharing in feed-forward neurons, supported by correlational and causal evidence, and (iii) an alignment-transfer dissociation, where cross-lingual transfer remains essentially unchanged despite higher alignment. Moreover, transfer is significantly lower for cross-script bilinguals even under fair vocabulary allocation, indicating that the script barrier is not merely a tokenizer artifact. All of our checkpoints and code are publicly available.

papers.title: LesionAgent: Training-Free Agentic Tumor Tracking and Response Assessment in Longitudinal CT
papers.abstract_en: Every few months, a cancer patient's CT scans decide whether treatment continues. 3D foundation models can now detect, segment, register and track lesions, yet none of them reads the scans as a radiologist does. A radiologist decides which findings are lesions, which are the same lesion months later and whether a new spot means progression, and checks each decision against the extensive rules of a clinical guideline. We introduce LesionAgent, an LLM agent that performs this read end to end without task-specific training. It operates frozen 3D models as tools, acts in 3D through coordinate-labelled views, remembers every lesion across visits in a registry, verifies every model output it relies on, and leaves every number to a deterministic guideline engine. On four public longitudinal CT datasets, LesionAgent tracks more lesions and measures them more accurately than every automatic baseline, and where the same 3D models chained by fixed rules call progression falsely at 33 of 56 follow-ups, it does so twice. On clinical follow-up CTs, it agrees with the radiologists' response at 20 of 23 follow-ups, including every change in response, and without training on DeepLesion, it retrieves more of its lesions than every tracker trained on it (89.0% vs. 87.4%). Its harness, not its LLM, makes the difference: given the same LLM and 3D models but not the harness, Claude Code reaches a detection F1 of 41% and LesionAgent 78%, and an open-weight LLM that can run inside the hospital rises from 6% to 73%. LesionAgent and a napari reading app for any LLM are available at https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/LesionAgent.

papers.title: ENC-QA: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Vision-Language Models on Electronic Navigational Charts
papers.abstract_en: Nautical charts encode safety-critical maritime information through standardized symbols, attributes, text, and heterogeneous geometries. Interpreting these charts and assessing the navigational significance of successive chart updates requires recognizing nautical features, determining their spatial relationships, and applying navigational knowledge. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer a promising approach to nautical-chart interpretation, yet systematic evaluation of their fine-grained nautical feature recognition, chart-based spatial reasoning, and application of navigational knowledge to assessing chart changes remains limited. We introduce ENC-QA, a diagnostic benchmark comprising 77,312 questions derived from 6,612 National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Electronic Navigational Charts (ENCs). The benchmark evaluates four complementary capabilities: ENC Perception, Spatial Reasoning, Joint Perception and Spatial Reasoning, and Application. Of these, 8,227 questions form a progressive subset that decomposes selected chart-change cases into linked questions progressing from change detection to criticality assessment, enabling case-level analysis of how models use perceptual and spatial evidence to determine the navigational significance of chart changes. Evaluations of 10 open-weight VLMs reveal substantial limitations in fine-grained nautical feature recognition and feature-grounded spatial reasoning. Controlled evidence interventions show that relevant perceptual and spatial information improves change-criticality accuracy. Our findings establish ENC-QA as a diagnostic resource for nautical-chart understanding and safety-critical navigational decisions. We will release the benchmark and evaluation code upon publication.

papers.title: MoHA: Model-Conditioned Harness Adaptation for Long-Video Agents
papers.abstract_en: Long-video understanding increasingly relies on agentic systems that actively acquire evidence rather than process fixed video representations. Their execution harnesses must coordinate language-level planning with video-level observation and evidence acquisition, yet are typically fixed across model stacks. We therefore introduce MoHA, a framework for model-conditioned harness adaptation that adapts a common initial execution harness to the specific planner and observer models it hosts. MoHA treats the harness itself as a model-conditioned optimization object: under the same task distribution and initialization, different planner-observer stacks can benefit from different executable harnesses. Starting from a common initial harness, MoHA analyzes failed calibration traces to diagnose model-harness mismatches and adapts both planner-side reasoning support, such as overview, memory, and verification, and observer-side capability assignments, including OCR and ASR specialists. After structural adaptation, MoHA separately calibrates observer execution configurations for the hosted model stack. Across three frozen planner stacks, MoHA improves Video-MME Full accuracy by 6.2-27.1 percentage points and Video-Holmes accuracy by 3.1-20.1 points over the fixed initial harness. Cross-model transfer further shows that the adapted harnesses generalize only partially to other models, highlighting the harness as a model-conditioned optimization layer for long-video understanding. papers.title: MetaRigor: From Agentic Automation to Verifiable End-to-End Meta-Analysis Through Scientific Decision Boundaries
papers.abstract_en: Automated meta-analysis requires not only accurate numerical extraction but also the consistent preservation of result identity across stages, including the associated study, comparison, population, outcome, time point, and analysis conditions. We present MetaRigor, an LLM workflow framework for verifiable end-to-end evidence synthesis. MetaRigor organizes study results as Study x Target units and operationalizes scientific decision boundaries at the task level through Task Contracts, programmatic rules, and source binding. The model performs semantic interpretation that depends on study context, whereas programs execute formalizable rules, computations, validation, and source verification. We conducted controlled evaluations across five stages: evidence acquisition, data extraction, risk of bias assessment, certainty of evidence assessment, and manuscript generation. MetaRigor achieved an F1 score of 86.29% for complete result delivery and 80.20% agreement for domain-level certainty of evidence judgments. Generated manuscripts received scores of 86.00 under human evaluation, exceeding all three baselines. A seven-case downstream end-to-end evaluation further yielded an aggregate F1 score of 77.01%, exceeding the strongest baseline by 9.78 percentage points. Cross-system tracing of archived outputs from three systems further showed that local mismatches or omissions in result identity could alter statistical inputs and the objects subjected to risk of bias assessment, with these errors subsequently propagating into the final report. Ablation experiments showed that task constraints and programmatic rules played distinct roles across different stages. These findings indicate that, in LLM-driven evidence synthesis workflows, consistently maintaining explicit result identity, decision boundaries, and provenance relationships is critical to improving end-to-end verifiability.

papers.title: Learning Inside Types: Epistemic Typestates for Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract_en: Type disciplines make programs safe by construction: components checked against each other's types compose into programs that cannot go wrong in the ways the types exclude. Types suit reinforcement learning: a type constrains what an agent may choose, not how it chooses, so the guarantee holds for every policy a learner produces. We introduce epistemic typestates, a type discipline for safe multi-agent reinforcement learning. An agent's type is a protocol whose states record its beliefs, the worlds it cannot rule out from its own observations and actions, and permits only actions that are safe in every world of the belief, whatever the others do within their public types. Agents learn inside their types, which are built and checked one agent at a time and run without communication. We prove type soundness and team safety, give a synthesis that is sound and complete, build types from guards when worlds are infinite, and show that shields are a special case. All proofs are mechanised in Rocq. On nine benchmarks, no typed learner causes a safety violation, and task performance does not differ significantly from that of two recent multi-agent shielding methods. papers.title: Beyond Math, Code, and Logic: Do Reasoning Models Transfer to Scientific Argumentation?
papers.abstract_en: Scientific discourse depends on argumentative reasoning: identifying claims, evaluating evidence, and constructing coherent responses. While recent advances in reasoning-capable language models have demonstrated strong performance on mathematical, coding, and logical benchmarks, their ability to engage in scientific argumentation remains unclear. We present the first systematic evaluation of language models across seven tasks spanning argument mining, rebuttal generation, and discourse-level reasoning using research papers, peer reviews, and grant proposals. Our study reveals that even frontier models with strong general reasoning skills struggle with domain-specific argumentative tasks, highlighting a fundamental capability gap. To address this, we introduce a training framework that explicitly scaffolds the argumentative reasoning process in language models, substantially improving their competence in scientific discourse. The resulting compact models approach or exceed the performance of much larger proprietary systems and generalize to unseen conversational settings, demonstrating reasoning transfer beyond task-specific supervision. These findings underscore that effective scientific argumentation is not an emergent property of scale, but requires explicit reasoning-aware training, and they point toward practical pathways for building AI systems that can contribute meaningfully to scientific discourse.

papers.title: DistDNA: Language Model Fingerprinting under Stochastic Decoding
papers.abstract_en: Behavioral fingerprints identify a large language model (LLM) from its responses to a shared set of prompts, enabling applications such as verifying whether a deployed model corresponds to the checkpoint it claims to be. Deployed models, however, are commonly served with stochastic decoding, under which the same model may produce different responses to an identical prompt, depending on an unknown temperature and top-$p$ setting. Existing representations such as LLM DNA provide limited treatment of this variation. A natural remedy is to characterize models by their response distributions, which, however, raises two challenges. First, each distribution must be estimated from only a small number of sampled responses. Second, a change in decoding setting can alter responses to the same extent as a change of checkpoint. Consequently, fingerprint distances alone provide an incomplete basis for model identity, and identification typically relies on a classifier trained jointly on fingerprints from many checkpoints. We propose DistDNA, which represents a model by its prompt-conditional response distributions and compares models by promptwise maximum mean discrepancy (MMD). The model under examination is assigned to the known checkpoint whose reference fingerprints, collected at several decoding settings, lie nearest to its own, without training a classifier. We show that finite sampling adds variance-dependent terms to the expected squared fingerprint distance, with these terms decreasing as $O(1/R)$ for equal response counts, where $R$ is the number of responses per prompt. Experiments across 115 model checkpoint entries demonstrate that DistDNA improves identification accuracy over the strongest baseline, LLM DNA, by 10.36%.

papers.title: Fix Where It Fails: Root-Cause-Guided Agentic Harness Optimization for Scene Graph Generation
papers.abstract_en: Scene graph generation (SGG) aims to detect objects in an image and predict the relationships between them. The standard PredCls, SGCls, and SGDet settings show how much performance drops without ground-truth boxes and labels, but not where or why a model fails. Knowing this would allow fixing a model where it fails, without retraining. We propose RoHa-SGG (Root-cause-guided Harness optimization for SGG), which extends agentic harness optimization to SGG. It optimizes the harness, the inference code around a frozen SGG model. RoHa-SGG has two main LLM agents. A root-cause analysis (RCA) agent finds the components where the model fails and diagnoses why, and a proposer agent searches for a harness that fixes these causes. We evaluate RoHa-SGG on Visual Genome and PSG with representative two-stage, one-stage, and multimodal-LLM SGG models. The analysis shows that the components where ground-truth triplets are lost differ across models and datasets. RoHa-SGG improves every metric on all five model-dataset combinations. Graph-constrained R@100 and mR@100 rise by up to 15.8 and 26.4 points for the multimodal LLM and by up to 3.6 and 10.1 points for the two-stage and one-stage models. With root-cause guidance, the harness search reaches the final score of an unguided search up to three times faster.

papers.title: Refrain: Learning Multi-Shot Consistency from Inconsistent References for A$^2$O Video Generation
papers.abstract_en: A comic-book character, a photorealistic cityscape, an oil-painted coffee cup -- such stylistically diverse references provide visual guidance across shots and frames, yet generating a coherent multi-shot video that unifies their visual styles while preserving subject identities and scene content remains challenging. Existing methods maintain cross-shot continuity through additional attention control or memory processing. However, they struggle to resolve disparate per-shot styles or handle reference-target duration mismatches within a single framework. We introduce Refrain, a unified model that learns cross-shot consistency through a self-supervised reconstruction task. Reference clips from the same original video are deliberately perturbed with distinct visual edits, and the model recovers the unedited source footage under a shared style prompt. The resulting pipeline yields DurMix-300K, which pairs independently edited references of varying durations with their original videos. Operating on the A$^2$O principle (Any Reference, Any Duration, One Timeline), Refrain maps image and video references onto a shared temporal canvas without auxiliary conditioning modules. For evaluation, experiments show that standard CLIP or DINO metrics frequently overlook stylistic clashes or misinterpret intended narrative cuts as inconsistency. We propose Shot-Debiased Consistency (SDC), which uses an extensive real-video bank to establish a baseline for style variation associated with content changes within shots. By discounting this baseline divergence, SDC evaluates cross-shot style shifts against real-world distributions, where smaller residual differences indicate higher stylistic continuity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Refrain achieves state-of-the-art performance in cross-shot consistency, while excelling at shot timing, reference adherence, and text alignment.

papers.title: Non-penetrating World Models
papers.abstract_en: We study a new problem of preventing object penetration in interactive video world models. To understand how existing models handle this, we introduce NoPeBench, a benchmark that evaluates how world models respond to physical obstacles. Our evaluation reveals that none of the open-source models can reliably prevent such failures. Surprisingly, however, these models already encode the information needed to predict such violations. We find that the hidden states of diffusion transformers (DiTs) can predict whether a candidate action will penetrate an obstacle. Building on this, we introduce NoPeWorld, a lightweight framework that detects and prevents penetration. Specifically, we train a small prediction head on top of a frozen DiT's hidden states to read out if a candidate action is safe or not. Unsafe actions are then replaced with safe ones that best preserve the original intent. Despite its simplicity, NoPeWorld substantially reduces the physical violation rate, averaged over six video world models, from 74% to 16%. Remarkably, our method shows zero-shot generalization to open-domain imagery, third-person viewpoints, and moving obstacles. We publicly release our code, the NoPeBench benchmark, and model weights. papers.title: Beyond Self-Critique: Epistemic Convergence Control for Multi-Agent Research Verification
papers.abstract_en: Multi-agent systems for scientific claim verification increasingly rely on role-structured LLM debate to pressure-test hypotheses. However, when debating agents are instantiated from the same underlying base model, they share identical latent representations, making self-critique bias structurally inevitable. Static fixed-iteration protocols compound this by either halting prematurely before evidence stabilizes or wasting inference compute after convergence. We present \sys{}, a multi-agent research verification framework that addresses both failure modes. First, we introduce an asymmetric role architecture comprising an Advocate, Skeptic, and Arbitrator with opposing epistemic directives, producing significantly lower role-embedding similarity (0.852 vs.\ 0.918 for symmetric Multi-Agent Debate [MAD], $p = 5.82 \times 10^{-8}$) and surfacing more contested claims (22.0\% vs.\ 15.4\%). Second, we propose the Belief-Delta ($\DB$) convergence criterion, an evidence-grounded stopping rule that eliminates over-iteration (0.0\% vs.\ 62.5\% for Fixed-$3$) while cutting LLM calls by 2.4$\times$. Third, each supported claim is anchored to a verbatim literature snippet audited by an independent NLI classifier, achieving a 21.7\% hallucination rate (comparable to 25.9\% for a Self-Refine critic, $p = 0.61$) while establishing auditable evidence grounding. Across 200 runs on 40 research hypotheses evaluated with DeepSeek-R1-32B, \sys{} balances compute efficiency with rigorous epistemic verification.

papers.title: SLICR: Strategy Logic-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract_en: Specification-guided reinforcement learning (RL) translates formal specifications of desired behavior of agents into shaped rewards. This paper introduces SLICR, a significant paradigm shift that advances the state of the art to specification-guided RL in adversarial settings under partial observability. We employ Strategy Logic (SL), which allows explicit quantification over agents' strategies and uses the linear temporal logic (LTL) to specify the agents' objectives and constraints. This enables reasoning not only about how agents should act to satisfy a specification, but also about how they should respond to the strategies and behaviors of other agents. We evaluate SLICR on three popular benchmarks: Predator-Prey, Google Research Football, and our home-grown extension of SMAC-HARD, demonstrating its effectiveness, scalability, and ability to adapt to diverse adversarial strategies.

papers.title: Turnout: Adaptive Attention Switching for Efficient Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Post-hoc transformer linearization replaces the key-value cache of full attention, which grows linearly with generation length, with a fixed size state. This change reduces memory consumption but often hurts accuracy. In reasoning tasks, which require long generations, this effect is especially pronounced. In this work we introduce Turnout, a method that mitigates accuracy loss as a result of linearization, while maintaining its memory-reduction benefits. We apply post-hoc linearization to a pretrained full-attention model, training a linear path through distillation while leaving the original full-attention path unchanged. During response generation, the resulting hybrid model retains both paths and uses a learned policy to control when each layer switches from full to linear attention. We train the policy with reinforcement learning using a reward that balances answer correctness and memory use. Empirical evaluation of our method shows that the learned adaptive policy achieves a better accuracy-efficiency Pareto frontier on reasoning tasks compared to fixed switching and static hybrid baselines.

papers.title: DPMA: Learning to Compress Mixture-of-Experts Models
papers.abstract_en: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures offer high computational efficiency, but storing all experts requires substantial memory and limits deployment on resource-constrained hardware. Most retraining-free MoE compression methods commit to either pruning or merging experts, often with a uniform compression ratio across layers. We introduce DPMA (Differentiable Prune Merge Absorb), which jointly learns compression operations and layer-wise expert allocation through gradient descent under a global expert budget. Separate learnable coefficients allow DPMA to prune experts, merge their parameters, and absorb their routing contributions by forwarding routing weights to retained experts. These coefficients and expert assignments are optimised to match the original model's outputs on calibration data while its weights remain frozen. Across four MoE models, eight multiple-choice benchmarks, and five compression ratios, DPMA achieves the highest accuracy averaged over benchmarks and compression ratios on each model among the evaluated methods. At $75\%$ expert reduction, it outperforms the strongest baseline on every model, with gains of up to $6.7$ percentage points.

papers.title: Benchmarks' Last Exam
papers.abstract_en: Public benchmarks guide model selection, post-training rewards and claims of progress in artificial intelligence, yet leaderboards report aggregate scores without verifying whether each task's prompt, environment and grader agree on what counts as success. How often that agreement fails in contemporary evaluations, and in which direction confirmed defects move scores, has remained unmeasured across grading designs. Here we synthesize task-level quality reviews of 749 tasks across eight frontier benchmarks and 767 public model evaluations spanning closed-form question answering, document rubrics and agentic execution to assess whether prompts, environments and graders align. Task validity stratifies sharply by grading architecture. Closed-form benchmarks revised after public error reporting reach 92.5% verified validity, compared with 29.3% across six multi-step suites that nevertheless already supply 161 verified complex tasks. Rubric suites fail through mismatches between prompts and reference checklists, whereas execution harnesses add incomplete state assertions, shared-channel leaks and grading-time collisions. Across confirmed defects, 71.7% withhold credit from compliant solutions while 28.3% permit shortcut passes, indicating that raw leaderboard ceilings understate frontier capability on many practical tasks. Grading committed patches inside a fresh container cuts confirmed runtime bypasses from 14.7% in shared containers to 2.7% (a 5.5x drop, and 0% in read-only or static suites), showing how targeted maintenance restores existing benchmarks at low cost. As the initial milestone of the long-term Benchmarks' Last Exam initiative, this synthesis launches sustained expansion across wider benchmark coverage and deeper evaluation-quality dimensions so that pursuing leaderboard gains directly advances genuine model capability.

papers.title: Tasklets: A Unit-Test Benchmark for Language Model Architectures

papers.title: Speculative Decoding Is Less Speculative Than You Think
papers.abstract_en: Speculative decoding accelerates language-model inference by preparing candidate continuations before the target model generates them. Its efficiency depends on how well limited drafting computation anticipates the path the target will actually follow. Anticipating this path involves two sources of uncertainty: the target model's predictions and the randomness of sampling. Yet the former requires a target-model forward pass, while the latter can be fixed before drafting. Building on this observation, we introduce DICE (Draw-Informed Candidate Selection), which pre-samples and synchronizes verification randomness across drafting and verification. By combining these known draws with predictions from an existing drafter, DICE allocates computation toward continuations more likely to be used in the current sampling run. This principle guides node selection throughout draft-tree construction and extends to asynchronous prefetching, where DICE predicts which next-round drafts to prepare. Without additional drafter training or changes to the target sampling distribution, DICE achieves state-of-the-art decoding throughput across diverse settings, with speedups of up to 24.6pp over strong baselines.
